description: Fig. 6 is a single schematic panel (no axes, no units, no scale bar, no printed numeric values) depicting the architecture/working principle of the Extra Trees ensemble model. A green rounded box at the top, labelled "Extra trees", is the origin of the diagram; dashed fan-out arrows connect it to three drawn decision trees plus a centred horizontal ellipsis ("…"), indicating that an arbitrary number N of trees is generated. Each tree is drawn as a small hierarchy of circles: one orange root node at the top, blue and orange internal split nodes, and blue or yellow terminal (leaf) nodes at the bottom. Underneath, white rectangular labels read "Tree 1", "Tree 2" and "Tree N". A dashed arrow from each tree points to a pink/red rounded box labelled "Result 1", "Result 2" and "Result N" respectively. Dashed arrows from every Result box converge on a green rounded box labelled "Majority voting", and a single solid arrow then points downward to the words "Final result". The figure therefore illustrates the ensemble mechanism: many independently grown extra trees each emit a prediction, and those outputs are combined by majority voting into one final prediction. The meaning of the node colours is not explained anywhere in the figure.

subfigures.description: Green rounded box labelled "Extra trees" from which dashed arrows fan out to three schematic decision trees and to a central horizontal ellipsis, indicating N constituent trees.

Three small decision-tree diagrams, each with an orange circular root node, blue/orange internal nodes and blue/yellow leaf nodes, labelled below as "Tree 1", "Tree 2" and "Tree N"; each tree feeds a pink rounded box labelled "Result 1", "Result 2" and "Result N".
Green rounded box labelled "Majority voting" receiving dashed arrows from all Result boxes, with one solid arrow leading down to the text "Final result".

observations.observation: The figure is a hierarchical block schematic: a green rounded box labelled "Extra trees" sits at the top and dashed arrows fan out from it to multiple individual decision-tree diagrams.
Each constituent decision tree is drawn as circles: an orange root node at the top, blue and orange internal split nodes, and blue or yellow leaf nodes at the bottom.
The trees are labelled "Tree 1", "Tree 2" and "Tree N", with a horizontal ellipsis between Tree 2 and Tree N showing that the number of trees N is arbitrary/not fixed.
Each tree is connected by a dashed arrow to a pink/red rounded box labelled "Result 1", "Result 2" or "Result N".
Dashed arrows from all Result boxes converge on a green rounded box labelled "Majority voting", which is followed by one solid arrow pointing down to "Final result".
No axes, units, scale bars, gridlines or printed numeric values appear anywhere in Fig. 6.
The colour coding of the tree nodes (orange, blue, yellow) carries no visible legend or explanation in the figure.
The caption states only that Fig. 6 shows the extra trees model structure, without describing any panel or value.
The citing text states that among seven machine learning models trained simultaneously the Extra Trees model performed best, with RMSE 76.2 MPa, MAPE 9.8 % and R2 of 0.978.
The citing text states that the Extra Trees model can serve as an effective supplement to the new YS prediction model, and that its specific structure is shown in Fig. 6.
The figure shows the aggregation step as majority voting of the individual tree results, i.e. the final prediction is a vote-based combination rather than an average shown on the diagram.
